name: satvikgosai/genea-web
content:
# genea-web

A privacy-first genealogy tool. Build and explore family trees visually from
GEDCOM files — everything runs locally in a single self-contained binary with no
external services and no account.

- **Local-first** — your data lives in a SQLite file on your machine, nothing is
  sent anywhere.
- **Single binary** — the Vue frontend is embedded into the Go server at compile
  time; deploy one file.
- **Standards-based** — import and export plain [GEDCOM](https://www.gedcom.org/)
  so your tree moves freely between Ancestry, MyHeritage, FamilySearch, and here.

## Features

- Import, edit, and export family trees in GEDCOM format
- Interactive tree visualization powered by Graphviz (WASM)
- Granular editing — people, relationships, children, and arbitrary GEDCOM facts
- A relationship finder (how is person A related to person B?)
- Persistent storage in a local SQLite database
- Light / dark / system theming

## Tech stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Backend | Go + [Gin](https://gin-gonic.com/), `log/slog` structured logging |
| Database | SQLite via [`modernc.org/sqlite`](https://pkg.go.dev/modernc.org/sqlite) (pure Go, no CGO) |
| GEDCOM | [`github.com/cacack/gedcom-go`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/v2) |
| Frontend | Vue 3 + [Vuetify 3](https://vuetifyjs.com/), built with Vite |
| Graph render | [`@hpcc-js/wasm-graphviz`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@hpcc-js/wasm-graphviz) |

## Requirements

- Go 1.25+ (see [`go.mod`](go.mod))
- Node.js 22 (see [`.nvmrc`](.nvmrc); `nvm use` picks the right version)
- [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/) (provided by `corepack enable`)

## Quickstart

```bash
# Build the full app (frontend + backend) into a single binary
make build

# Run
./bin/genea-web
```

Then open [http://localhost:8080](http://localhost:8080).

## Configuration

Copy [`.env.example`](.env.example) to `.env` to override locally; both Vite (at
build time) and the Go binary (at startup) read from it.

| Variable        | Default      | Description                                          |
|-----------------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `PORT`          | `8080`       | HTTP listen port                                     |
| `DATABASE_PATH` | `genea.db`   | Path to the SQLite database file                     |
| `GIN_MODE`      | `release`    | `release` for JSON logs / prod; otherwise text logs  |
| `VITE_API_BASE` | `/api`       | API base path baked into the frontend at build time  |
| `VITE_DEBUG`    | `false`      | Enables developer affordances in the UI              |

## Development

```bash
# One-time: build the frontend so the Go server has something to embed
make frontend

# Two terminals:
make dev-be    # Go server (recompiles on restart)
make dev-fe    # Vite HMR on :5173 (proxies /api to the backend)

# Quality gates
make lint          # eslint + golangci-lint
make format        # prettier + gofmt/goimports
make test          # vitest + go test ./...
make test-coverage
```

`make dev-be` depends on `cmd/server/dist/` existing because of `go:embed` — run
`make frontend` once before the first `make dev-be`.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full command reference and code
conventions, and [`web/README.md`](web/README.md) for the frontend in detail.

## Docker

```bash
make docker          # builds genea-web:latest from a multi-stage Dockerfile
docker run -p 8080:8080 genea-web:latest
```

The build is three stages (Node → Go → `scratch`), so the final image is just
the static binary. The binary has a built-in `--healthcheck` flag, and the
Dockerfile's `HEALTHCHECK` invokes it directly — no shell required in the
`scratch` image.

## API

The HTTP API is JSON over `/api`. Every response carries an `X-Request-ID`
header so backend log lines can be correlated to a request, and 4xx/5xx bodies
include the same id under `request_id`. The backend is authoritative: it owns
GEDCOM parsing/serialization and all validation. IDs are UUID v4 strings, and
the total request body is capped at 10 MB.

| Method | Path                                    | Description                                  |
|--------|-----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| GET    | `/healthz`                              | Liveness + DB ping (200 ok / 503 down)       |
| GET    | `/api/trees`                            | List saved trees (summaries)                 |
| POST   | `/api/trees`                            | Create an empty tree → `{ id }`              |
| POST   | `/api/import?name=…`                    | Import a raw GEDCOM body → `{ id }`          |
| GET    | `/api/trees/:id`                        | Fetch the full tree document                 |
| GET    | `/api/trees/:id/gedcom`                 | Export the tree as a downloadable `.ged`     |
| PUT    | `/api/trees/:id`                        | Rename a tree (and optional icon)            |
| DELETE | `/api/trees/:id`                        | Delete a tree (cascades)                     |
| POST   | `/api/trees/:id/persons`                | Create a person                              |
| PUT    | `/api/persons/:id`                      | Update a person's core columns               |
| PUT    | `/api/persons/:id/facts`                | Replace a person's fact tree                 |
| DELETE | `/api/persons/:id`                      | Delete a person (+ collapse empty families)  |
| POST   | `/api/trees/:id/families`               | Create a relation (partner1 + optional 2)    |
| DELETE | `/api/families/:id`                     | Delete a family                              |
| POST   | `/api/families/:id/children`            | Add a child                                  |
| DELETE | `/api/families/:id/children/:pid`       | Remove a child                               |
| DELETE | `/api/families/:id/partners/:pid`       | Remove a partner (deletes family if empty)   |

Import lives at `/api/import` (not `/api/trees/import`) to avoid colliding with
the `/api/trees/:id` parameterized route. Date validation runs only on values a
user actually changes, so a non-standard date carried in from an import never
blocks an unrelated edit; partner and child links must reference a person in the
same tree.

## Architecture

A single Go binary serves both the JSON API and the embedded Vue SPA.

```
cmd/server/         Entry point: loads config, builds the Gin engine, embeds dist/
internal/
  db/               SQLite pool + versioned migrations (embedded .sql files)
  store/            Transactional data-access layer, split by aggregate
  gedcom/           GEDCOM <-> TreeDocument mapping, date + continuation handling
  graph/            Whole-tree graph model + DOT serialization
  handlers/         Gin handlers + middleware (RequestID, slog, MaxBodySize, SPA)
  models/           Shared DTOs (TreeDocument / Person / Family / Fact)
web/                Vue 3 + Vite frontend (see web/README.md)
```

**Single-binary embed.** The Vite build writes to `cmd/server/dist/`, which
`main.go` embeds with `//go:embed dist`. (Go's embed directive can't use `..`,
which is why Vite's `outDir` points there rather than at a repo-root `dist/`.)
Unknown non-API paths fall back to `index.html` for client-side routing.

**Relational data model.** A tree is normalised rather than stored as one GEDCOM
blob. `persons` keeps denormalised core columns (name/sex/birth/death) for fast
list and caption rendering, while `facts` is a self-referencing tree that
preserves every other (possibly nested or custom) GEDCOM tag verbatim.

```
trees            (id, name, icon, created_at, updated_at)
persons          (id, tree_id, given_name, surname, sex, birth/death date+place, …)
families         (id, tree_id, created_at)
family_partners  (family_id, person_id, role)        -- HUSB / WIFE
family_children  (family_id, person_id, ordinal)
facts            (id, person_id?, family_id?, parent_fact_id?, tag, value, ordinal)
```

Every owning relationship uses `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so deleting a tree, person,
or family cleans up its dependents automatically.

**Migrations.** The schema is built from numbered files under
`internal/db/migrations/` (one table per file), embedded into the binary and
applied in lexical order. A `schema_migrations` ledger records what has run; each
migration and its ledger row are applied in a single transaction, so a failure
leaves neither a half-applied schema nor a false ledger entry. Migrations are
forward-only — change the schema by adding a new numbered file, never by editing
an existing one.

**Store layer.** One `Store` repository over the whole schema, with methods split
by aggregate (`store_trees.go`, `store_persons.go`, `store_families.go`,
`store_facts.go`). Every multi-step mutation runs inside a transaction so
structural edits stay consistent — e.g. deleting a person tears down any family
left without partners. Reads batch-load persons, families, partners, children,
and facts to avoid N+1 queries. All store calls use the request context, so a
cancelled request cancels its queries.

**GEDCOM.** The `gedcom` package maps the parser library's record model to/from
the app's `TreeDocument`. Import is lenient — a `RepairContinuations` pass folds
the literal newlines some real-world exporters embed in NOTE/TEXT values into
proper continuation lines so messy files still load — while edits are validated
strictly (impossible dates and a death before birth are rejected).

## Testing

```bash
make test
```

- **Backend** — `go test ./...`. Tests open `db.Init(":memory:")` (no file I/O);
  they cover the migration ledger/idempotency, FK cascades, GEDCOM round-trips
  over the sample files, date validation, and the REST API through the real HTTP
  layer.
- **Frontend** — Vitest over the API client (`web/tests/`). See
  [`web/README.md`](web/README.md).

## Project structure

```
cmd/server/main.go        Entry point + --healthcheck self-probe
internal/                 Go packages (db, store, gedcom, graph, handlers, models)
web/                      Vue 3 + Vite frontend
Dockerfile                Multi-stage build → FROM scratch
Makefile                  build / dev / test / lint / format / docker targets
.env.example              Committed config defaults
```
